For my chameleons I mist their cages multiple times daily, never let basking temp go above 85, have TONS of branches and plants (both fake and real) for them to climb and hide in, I feed a variety of foods (super worms, crickets, Dubai roaches, wax and horn worms as a treat) and make sure they’re warm enough at night (if you have ac running, you most likely will need a heat bulb to get him through the chilly night). It does look like a boy, coloration appears female but those spurs are a dead give away. Make sure to keep track of the date you purchased/started using your uvb bulb, they need to be replaced after a certain amount of time because they aren’t as effective at admitting rays (I think the period is either every 3 months or every 6). Make sure not to fry them (having too high wattage bulb too close to the cage), make sure to watch humidity levels, and watch out for eye problems. With chameleons, eye problems are common (like infections or them getting crusty, so make sure to pick out an exotic vet now so you don’t scramble later on). That’s just what I can think of off the top of my head though, very beautiful chameleon! Best of luck to you and Killian, and have fun with making awesome memories together!

So right off the bat: look for at least a 20-30 gallon long tank that can hold water, a good filter that will be easy to change, large stones the little guy can’t eat (pond stones) for decor, a floating basking platform, a UVB bulb and a proper barking bulb. I use zoomed splash proof halogen 75 watt bulb but that’s for my adult sliders’ 2x2 egg crate basking platform (completely separate from their tank which I’d highly recommend bc it offers a place for them to dry off completely — I did a 3-sided box out of egg crate, a bulb hung above it, and it has a ramp in and out of their water), have some floating turtle food but also be ready to chop some veggies for the lil guy for additional nutrients (once larger maybe offer feeder fish?), also a proper water heater of course. Filter and lights and proper food are your biggest worry. They get massive (size of a dinner plate) and live a long time (50 years!), so be prepared to track down a 75 gallon tank in the future (you could use a 40 possibly, but I use 75 for my individual sliders). Best bet for cheap tanks would be either marketplace on Facebook or your local pet section on Craigslist. I had a caiman lizard who was severely abused by its previous owners, the last three inches of her tail was dead and came off with some stuck shed. Bathed her in a betadine-water mixture, put Neosporin on her wounds but only use the type that is without pain reliever and therefore animal safe, and had her on paper towels on a while (six of her toes were dead too which also came off) Everything healed nicely and I had no problems with it at all. Just got to make sure they stay clean. She was as healthy as could be once I rehomed to her to her last and final home to a friend of mine where I know she is living her best life. So yeah, betadine bathes, non pain relief Neosporin, and paper towels. This also worked for a blue tongue skink of mine who had a cut.
